text:
Seven straight losses ended in Las Vegas last night, and the Canucks get about 24 hours to enjoy it. Filip Chytil scored twice in a 6-3 win over the Golden Knights, and now Manny Malhotra's team plays the second night of a back-to-back in Salt Lake City. One win doesn't move the bigger picture much: Vancouver has 9 points from 22 games, and our playoff simulations give it about a one-in-a-thousand shot at the postseason. At five on five the Canucks take 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and they didn't win the chance battle in any of their last five games, last night included.

That's why the loudest Vancouver story is about who might leave. Elias Pettersson has been the most written-about Canuck for two weeks, and Jake DeBrusk's name is in the trade columns too, with Markerzone.com and NHL Trade Rumors both reporting that the Canucks are firm on their asking price. Pettersson, for his part, has points in four straight. Brock Boeser has points in seven straight and reached 500 for his career last week.

Utah's problem is the opposite one. The Mammoth take 57% of the five-on-five expected goals and are winless in five (0-2-3), including a 6-5 shootout loss to San Jose on Saturday after leading by two. Karel Vejmelka, projected to start, is 6.11 goals below expected this season after finishing last year 5.39 above, and KSL Sports ran the headline "He has a job to do." The lineup is thin, too: Dylan Guenther is on injured reserve until about Dec. 5, Nick Schmaltz and Nate Schmidt are out, and Vincent Trocheck, acquired from the Rangers in the summer, has slid beside Clayton Keller and is playing more than 25 minutes a night. He is one assist from 400.

The good news for Utah is that Logan Cooley, who had 13 points in his last 10 before he got hurt, is off the out list and day-to-day. Our numbers make this lopsided in the chances, 3.82 expected goals for Utah to 2.55. Vancouver's starter hadn't been confirmed when we wrote this.
headline: Canucks snap the skid, then face a wounded Utah
